newsitem.title: FRANCE: France said wanting "ambitious" payment from EDF.
newsitem.headline: France said wanting "ambitious" payment from EDF.

text.p: The French government has called on the EDF electricity utility to "set itself ambitious targets for reimbursements to the state" in business plans which the EDF has to prepare for 1997 onwards, a CGT trade union official said on Thursday.
The Communist-led CGT union issued a copy of a note from the finance and industry ministries dated July 12.
Neither ministry was immediately able to offer comment or an explanation on what kind of payments were at stake when they were contacted by Reuters.

Two newspapers have recently suggested the government was looking to increase contributions from the state electricity utility to help bolster state finances under the tight public deficit constraints implied by European monetary union.

France got European Union approval on Thursday to use a transfer of 37.5 billion francs from France Telecom -- money it will have to use to cover future pension liabilities at the telecoms operator -- to help get its public deficit to the level of three percent of GDP next year which is called for by the Maastricht treaty to qualify for monetary union.
The CGT official said his union believed that its demand for a lowering of electricity prices would be compromised by any government plan to take more money out of the EdF.
